title: Sky Shield

selected_categories.reasoning: The core interaction is precision pointer shooting against appearing targets, with one weapon explicitly serving as a high-damage sniper-style shot. The player does not navigate space and instead eliminates targets from a fixed defensive viewpoint, which strongly matches sniper-gallery style play.

Enemies continuously arrive and must be eliminated before they leak through the defense, with lives acting as a base health resource. The game is not about placing defenses, but it clearly uses defend-the-line survival pressure.

The game uses aiming, shooting, weapon switching, reticle feedback, and real-time target elimination. However, it lacks player locomotion, 3D navigation, and a literal first-person world model, so this is only a partial mechanical fit.

The enemies are sci-fi hovering threats in a stylized neon defense setting, and the game is clearly a shooter. The foes are drones rather than confirmed aliens, so the category fits the arcade space-combat feel more than the exact fiction.

The run continues until shields are exhausted, and difficulty escalates indefinitely. Survival matters structurally, but the game lacks broader resource loops or exploration typically associated with the survival label.

uncertainty_notes: The game overlaps with several shooter subgenres but does not perfectly map to the provided category universe because it is a stationary arcade defense shooter rather than a traditional sniper sim, FPS, or tower defense game.
Tower defense was considered, but the absence of unit placement, lanes, and build strategy made Wave defense game the better defensive match.
Endless runner, lane runner, and other movement-centric categories were rejected because the player does not control movement at all.
The ranking favors interaction feel over theme-only labels.
